title: Launch a pizza from a peel onto an oven stone
instruction: Launch the pizza from the peel onto the oven stone.
context: Launching a topped pizza calls for a quick pull at the oven mouth. Once the leading edge reaches the stone, a short, sudden backward stroke draws the peel out while the soft dough settles flat and the toppings stay in place. The task combines precise insertion through a low opening with a timed transfer of support from the peel to the stone. Moving an oven rack tests rigid alignment, turning out a cake uses inversion, and preparing or slicing pizza tests food preparation.
setup: Use a cold, unfuelled Ooni Karu 12 with the door off, its 330 × 330 × 15 mm cordierite stone and a stock 505 × 305 × 12 mm bamboo peel. Place a level 500 × 460 mm hardwood prep worktop 10 mm in front of the oven mouth and 2–3 mm above the stone. Lay the peel flat, pointing into the oven. Center the blade at (285, 0) mm in station coordinates. Start a 240 mm raw dough round 46 mm toward the leading edge, topped with four 28 mm pepperoni slices on a 116 mm square. See the README for the bench height, coordinates and preparation.
scoring: Score 0.5 if the peel carries the crust through the mouth and the complete crust rests flat on the stone with the peel clear. The crust may extend at most 3 mm beyond a stone edge, must span at least 208 mm along each axis, and must sit within 28 mm of the stone height. Score 1.0 if these conditions hold, the crust bounding rectangle center is within 45 mm of the stone center, and all four slices rest on the crust with each slice center within 103 mm of the crust center. All other outcomes score zero. Check the trial video and use a ruler and inspection photo for the final state.
reset_notes: Use a fresh measured dough round each trial. Clear crumbs and dough from the cold stone and peel and reset the four toppings using the square layout.
fidelity: Full-size USD assets approximate the named oven and peel. A volumetric deformable crust bends under the load but does not tear. Rigid discs stand in for pepperoni. The dusted blade and dough use estimated friction, and the handle keeps its own contact material. The oven is cold.
scores: Dream-1: 0.0 (1,200-step limit). Scripted Inspect Robots demo: 1.0.
